chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade giving the butcher anything from the hides of the sacrificial animal and its collars/coverings.

key_terms.أَجْلَالِهَا: Collars or coverings of the animal

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forbid giving to the butcher from the sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the economic rights of the butcher in sacrificial rituals by prohibiting the payment of hides and collars (ajlal), ensuring that the primary value of the meat remains with the owner or the poor. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction highlights the principle that the butcher's wage is typically derived from the meat itself, preventing the depletion of the sacrificial asset's worth through the retention of durable by-products. This ruling underscores the Prophet's emphasis on equitable distribution and the specific stewardship of sacrificial resources.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade giving of the hide, collar and covering of the offering animals to the butchers.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn af-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited giving of the hide, collar and covering of offering animals to the butchers.”
